docs.title: The Black Circle
docs.text:
The Black Circle is a faction of mercenaries that formed in the beginning of the 3rd Age. Their ideals are centered around autonomy and individual freedoms, vowing to serve under no one ruler. There is no “Head of the Black Circle”, it is a loosely connected web of small chapterhouses and roaming bands. Due to their nature, they are in direct conflict with The Aegis Legion and are often vying for the sympathies of the average Sarosian. Most adventurers come out of, or have to try to get through the Black Circle at one time or another…

Unless formed in large numbers for a show of strength by coin, members of the Black Circle tend to blend in to normal crowds. Their attire is often dark and suited for life in the strange wilderness of Saros. Members are only truly identified by a small black circle tattoo on the inner forearm that each must bear upon joining. They greet with a sort of handshake by grabbing each other’s right arm near the elbow.

docs.text: The Prism is a draconic cult lead by madman Silas Voss and his right hand Malgrim Darkshade. The cult seeks the egg of a Multi-Chromatic Dragon, for they believe the old Sarosian legend that the first to be seen by a newborn Multi-Chromatic Dragon will be granted a wish of the most powerful magnitude.

docs.title: Malgrim Darkshade
docs.text: The right hand of Silas Voss and second in command of The Prism dragon cult. Malgrim is a tall and fair female Elf cloaked in all black and hooded to obscure her pale white hair and milk-white eyes. Her loyalty to Silas is a means to an end… she constantly seeks opportunities to expand her influence, seize control, and surpass her master and unravel the secrets of the forbidden esoteric magics.

docs.title: Silas Voss
docs.text:
When Caelum and Amara became aware of their student Silas’ malevolent machinations, it was too late… He had already began the ritual to open the rift to the outer planes, granting his wish for immortality while simultaneously dooming him.

Silas Voss’s immortality is shrouded in the Veil of Desolation, a curse that disconnects him from the fundamental energies of life. Unable to feel joy, love, or any positive emotion, he exists in a perpetual state of emotional desolation. The curse also taints his magical abilities, turning the benevolent spells he once wielded into conduits of despair and decay.

Driven by an insatiable desire to break free from this emotional abyss, Silas relentlessly searches for a cure. Rumors speak of an ancient artifact, hidden in the forgotten corners of Saros, that purportedly has the power to unravel the Veil of Desolation… a Multi-Chromatic Dragon’s egg.

docs.title: The Queen's Council
docs.text: A cabal of five of the most powerful influencers in all of Saros. Currently ruling the realm on behalf of Queen Amara from The Radiant Citadel in Pyrris. Some believe them to be behind her disappearance, while others praise them for keeping the realm afloat through such troubling times. While the former may be running on speculation, the latter are hoping flattery saves them from the Stonepeak stockades.

docs.title: A Brief Saros History
docs.text:
“Near Four thousand and two hundred years in the past, a formidable wizard named Caelum uttered a wish in desperation, seeking salvation for the remnants of his devastated people from the doomed choice of his greatest pupil. The wish, granted with a mysterious benevolence, whisked them away from their familiar realm of Mystara to an entirely uncharted continent — a pristine land they christened “Saros”. This new territory unfolded as a tapestry of richness, brimming with wonders, beauty, magic, and peril. Since their arrival, Saros has become the backdrop for countless fantastical tales, shared in hushed tones around campfires and echoing through the halls of hearths across the known world.

Whispers carried on the wind tell of a clandestine cult known simply as “The Prism”, sworn to ancient draconic rites, and veiled in secrecy. This enigmatic order is believed to harbor an insatiable desire for the power encapsulated within a Multi-Chromatic Dragon’s egg. Legend tells that such an egg possesses the potential to birth a dragon of unparalleled majesty, a force capable of shaping the fate of Saros: by granting the first to be seen by a newborn Multi-Chromatic Dragon… a wish!

At the heart of Saros stands Pyrris, the capital, with The Radiant White Citadel soaring into the clouds, vigilant over the waters of Bishop’s Bay. For epochs, The Citadel was under the rule of the Elven Queen Amara. However, over the last few months, an enigmatic shift occurred — the queen, once an ever direct presence in her kingdom, ceased personal interactions and began communicating solely through written decrees. Rumors wildly circulate, suggesting that she might have fallen ill, or that a coup occurred and she is imprisoned within the tower by The Council …maybe kidnapped by The Prism, or an even graver fate…”

Almost everywhere outside of civilization is very ancient and dangerous. Ancient warp-gates can be found and reactivated. Some may still work. No one knows for sure what lies beyond the seas. The elves call the planet “Aiy-Vana”, meaning “Beautiful to Behold”. The dwarves call the planet “Daron”, meaning “Deep Knowledge”. Rumors tell of werewolves that appear during red moons. There are twin suns in the sky.

docs.title: Ages of Saros
docs.text:
• 1st Age (The First Breaths) No actual historical record. Simply regarded as myth. Dragons ruled the lands before other beings came into existence, and it is believed that there was a great war that shaped much of the central region of Saros, namely “The Glimmering Expanse” and “The Wyrm Scar”.

  • 2nd Age (The Great Tribulation)  Magic was a mystery to the first humanoid beings to awaken on Saros. Mistrust and betrayals among early tribes of men caused massive wars leading to the beginning and end of factions like the Storm Knights and the creation of the “Urmong Barrows”. With the discovery of the magic of the Fey-Lines, the Elves took to cultivating the soil and disappeared into the forests, while the Dwarves struck the earth and maintained their stonework kingdoms throughout their “Delves”.

  • 3rd Age (Caelum’s Arrival) Caelum’s wish brought nearly 1000 beings to Saros. Their technology, agriculture, warfare, and general way of living introduced massive changes to the geopolitical and cultural landscape due to being such a more advanced peoples than the native Sarosians. This disparity between the old and new inhabitants drove the Elves to their secret woodland domains, while the dwarves have all but disappeared due to wars, diaspora, clan-fighting, and the immense danger that comes along with delving the depths of the underworld. Queen Amara has ruled over Saros for the last 800 years since Caelum’s death, but she has recently been missing and a great unrest is stirring across the land. The Council are overseeing Saros in Amara’s stead.

docs.title: The Great Betrayal
docs.text: After The Wandering when the first clans began to settle into their own territories, The Khaz’armok and Khaz’dar lords, once great friends, became sworn enemies. The discovery of the finest gem to have ever been seen in Saros caused a great rift and blood feud between them, and they waged a massive war to decide which clan would possess it, but both failed in the end, as it was stolen.

docs.title: The Spring Harvest Festival
docs.text:
Wonderful foods, lavish entertainment, and games of all sorts are plentiful during The Festival. The Spring Harvest is celebrated by most civilized peoples of Saros in their own ways, but the largest celebration is held annually at the Capitol in Pyrris.

A long standing tradition, predating even Queen Amara’s rule, it’s a busy time filled with anticipation, as ripened fruits are being collected and new seeds are planted with hopes of a bountiful fall harvest. Spring rains nourish the young plants, and farmers must be vigilant in protecting their crops from pests and disease. While also inventorying and delivering their goods to the Festival.

docs.title: The Wandering
docs.text: When the first Dwarves, the Khaz’um, set out to explore and chart the furthest reaches of Saros, what they found set their hearts ablaze with wonder and greed. Many small offshoot clans began forming at this time, as the dwarves would naturally settle where they found potent Fey-Lines. There was great cooperation between the dwarves, setting up Delves and other great cities, until eventually it dwindled down to only a few major clans, and most was peaceful and prosperous until The Great Betrayal.

docs.title: Fey Lines
docs.text: Loosely connected magical streams that seem to flow between one another and converge at specific points all across Saros. Where any lines meet there forms great places of magical energy that the elves use for creating and maintaining life, and the Dwarves use for the great Fey-stone found at the convergences.

docs.title: Fey stone
docs.text: A dull, grey, malleable rock rarely found where convergences of Fey-Lines intersect. When worked with the proper care and skill Leystone can be infused with magical properties.

docs.title: Golden Grouper
docs.text: Legend tells of a massive golden grouper the size of a whale somewhere out in the depths of Bishop’s Bay.

docs.title: Storm Knights
docs.text: A once great domain of early Sarosian man. The pinnacle of human advancement and achievement through use of esoteric Fey-Line magics and supposed developed psionic powers. Little is known of their history despite their ruins littering nearly every corner of Saros.

docs.title: The Great Sphinx
docs.text: A Great Sphinx is rumored to reside somewhere in the deep deserted region of The Glimmering Expanse. The Sphinx has the ability to grant wishes but only to those it deems “pure of heart”. It is said that the Sphinx speaks with a new voice every sentence, sometimes that of a child, sometimes that of a horrifying banshee, and even possibly your own…

docs.title: Caelum
docs.text: A powerful human wizard from Mystara who, in desperation, used “contact higher plane” to try and reach ANY being to free his people, and in doing so, ended up striking a deal with Bahamut. He gave up his immortality in exchange for transportation to “safety” where his people could live on, free from the vortex created by Silas Voss.

docs.title: Edric Vane
docs.text:
Edric Vane led one of the best-known expeditions from Port Quartz toward the Masys Mountains centuries ago.

Later retellings made him an uncomplicated frontier hero. Surviving records tell a harsher story.

Edric departed with approximately sixty people.

Seven returned.

docs.title: Legacy
docs.text:
The expedition:

  • Charted portions of the western river country
  • Recorded failed crossings
  • Recorded dependable landmarks, seasonal water levels, and several abandoned Second Age works
  • Described the difficult hills and river country west of Port Quartz
  • Marked a mountain jut and sheltered basin later used by expeditions traveling toward Masys
  • Lost members to terrain, creatures, disease, and unknown events

Several important journal pages are missing, but none of Edric’s surviving material refers to Rom or Mossback. Edric lived centuries before either came to the Masys region.

His descendant Hesta Vane serves as First Mooring and resists romantic versions of the expedition.

A weathered marker at Westwater Ferry still points toward Masys, though no road follows it.

docs.title: Rom The Wizard
docs.text: Legends tell of an old ancient and wise Wizard named Rom, who lives on the southern slopes of The Masys Mountain range, allegedly on the back of a giant snail…

docs.title: The Serpent King
docs.text: A once great ruler of the northern Goslow region, the Serpent King was besieged on all sides from many enemies. He was a fair and generous ruler who spent most of his resources trying to obtain immortality. He tasked his court wizard Xiximanter with discovering the fountain of youth, but died long before the wizard’s experiments concluded.

docs.title: Xiximanter
docs.text:
A centuries old Snake-Man Wizard… Xiximanter was left in his laboratory by The Serpent King to work on his time experiments, and unbeknownst to himself, succeeded. When he was found by a party of adventurers, it so happened that what seemed like a few days to him was actually hundreds of years in Saros. While he worked, his civilization crumbled around him and his once great culture has been left to history.

He currently lives in the Tomb of The Serpent King and is very friendly to most bipeds, usually willing to talk and negotiate deals if anyone seeks his knowledge of time manipulation. He absolutely HATES goblins and will become enraged at the sight of one unbound.

docs.title: Goslow
docs.text: The largest trade hub and hot-spot in all of Saros. Goslow is nestled on the inner coast of Bishop’s Bay, where larger ships must first weigh anchor and send smaller vessels to navigate the Breakwater Rocks and at last reach the docks. Goslow is the closest landing point and natural passthrough destination for anyone seeking entry up the High Road along the massive cliff to Pyrris.

docs.text: Located just outside the gates of Goslow on the coast of Bishop’s Bay to the north. The main marina and shipyard of of the Aucien Family.

docs.title: Bedford's Forge
docs.text:
Known for the finest craftsmanship this side of Vy’Tungavor, Bedford’s Forge is the local Goslow smithy where you can get anything you desire made if you are willing to both pay the high price, and wait patiently on the list behind high-priority clientele. Heat bellows out of the doorway and permeates the entire colossal structure of The Forge. Many humans tend to the forges that fill the interior, and the sounds of metal being worked drowns out all but the loudest voices.

Overseeing the forge is a massive man simply known as Bedford, one of the few known beings in Saros capable of working Fey-stone into useable weapons and armor.

docs.title: Duskpoint
docs.text: Captained by Vostin The Mighty, The Aegis Legion Garrison lies just outside the walls on the north side of Goslow at Duskpoint. Duskpoint serves as both the Legion’s Headquarters and the city’s police force and jailhouses.

docs.title: Temple of Torm
docs.text:
Korth serves as Head Priest of Torm at the temple. He is a very old and wise human paladin with large white eyebrows that hide his small eyes. Fairly narcoleptic and seems to always be asleep, however locals tell of a time when he was a mighty warrior who rallied the town to victory against a massive orc raiding horde.

Ostalda is the resident sage that lives in a small room attached to the library inside of the temple. She is a half-elf with dark hair and bluing skin from years of divining with sacred mushrooms.

docs.title: The Bulkhead
docs.text: Jarvis Aucien, a tall blonde and muscular Elf, operates The Bulkhead, a family rope and ship making business that has been passed down the Aucien line for generations.

docs.title: The Silver Drake
docs.text:
Overseen by Lone-Wolf Louie, The Silver Drake is one of the most famous Gambler’s Guild halls in all of Saros, 2nd only to the massive hall in Rore. The Silver Drake is a tightly ran and well secured building where the foolhardy come from all over Saros to test their luck and their coin with hopes of leaving Goslow as rich as Lord Goldhaven himself!

docs.title: The Sphinx's Spellbook
docs.text:
Just a few feet away from the Goslow docks sits The Sphinx’s Spellbook, an extremely narrow and cramped two story building that shows it’s age in cracked stonework from the overgrown roots and vines that seem to weave in and out of the entire structure. Inside the shop a dank haze fills the air… incense and herbal smoke mix with dust from the piles of parchment stacked in every corner. A small walkway through books and potions and various knick-knacks seems treacherous, but when braved, leads to a tiny counter with a bell.

The owner of the Sphinx is a short female half-elf named Mori; a timid but extremely intelligent young woman with purple hair and alchemical tattoos all over her visible skin - except her face which is almost free of ink. Mori lives above the shop on the 2nd story with her pet penguin Chibs, who she rescued and healed after finding him alone, lost, and hurt in Bishop’s Bay several years ago. Chibs wears a small magical frost rune pendant Mori made for him to keep his body chilly!

docs.title: The Toad
docs.text:
The Toad is a two-story half-timber and brick building with smooth stone floors and a warm breeze from the massive blazing fireplace that invites the weary traveler inside on a cold evening. The largest and busiest tavern and Inn in Goslow, filled with elf-wrought tables and chairs, it was once a massive mansion that fell to ruin with age and was bought and restored by Perla. The main hall houses a large collection of priceless artwork from all across Saros. Accommodations range from small, modestly priced rooms with a soft woolen mattress, to huge luxury suites that rival small houses.

The owner and innkeeper of the Toad is a tall female halfling named Perla. She was once an adventurer, but was maimed by a dragon and lost her left leg. She loves details and rumors, and she’s often seen sitting at a table sharing tall drinks and even taller tales with adventurers that come into the Toad.

The inn’s manager is a stocky female halfling named Gerdga. She has a heavy smoker’s cough, a dry sarcastic wit, and she insists on inspecting every coin paid to her. Anything you need can either be found behind her bar or by her hard working crew.

Employees: Hob - Bound water elemental who works as bouncer and cleaner. Lommen and Hommen - gnome twins given a job by Perla after they were rescued. Munchies Muldridge - Nephew of Gerdga and general clumsy fool.

Menu: Baked Goose and Onion, Glass of Mead (1 sp) Baked Shrimp and Almond Bread, Glass of Wine (2 sp) Vegetable soup and Garlic Bread, Choice of Wine (2 sp) Baked Phoenix and Boysenberry Tart, Glass of Brunae (3 sp)

    Overseeing Bedford’s Forge is a massive man simply known as Bedford. He has a loud booming voice, a shiny bald head, and a large grey mustache. He and his wife Mary love visitors and they are always cheerful. His leather overalls are covered in soot and burn marks and his hands are like chiseled steel from decades of dedicated smith-work. Though very bulky and freakishly strong, he is also a proficient artist who adorns his creations with delicate and detailed inlays. He is one of the few beings in all of Saros capable of forging Fey-stone.

Manager of The Toad. Always seen with a pipe in one hand and her magnifying glass in the other. She is a short halfling with a deep raspy voice and a horrible smoker’s cough. Gerdga’s best friend is Perla Mudridge, the owner of The Toad. Gerdga’s sarcastic and dry wit is rarely matched in all of Saros. She insists on inspecting every coin coming into The Toad to make sure of it’s authenticity.

docs.title: Hob
docs.text: Hob is a Water Elemental that stands 8 foot tall. He is the bouncer and servant at The Toad in Goslow. At Gerdga’s command, he sloshes through the bar, cleaning tables and kicking out unruly patrons… somehow leaving no trace of liquid behind. Hob doesn’t have feelings or desires, he is simply a magical construct who is bound to The Toad, and cannot leave it’s premises without turning back into plain water.

docs.title: Jarvis Aucien
docs.text:
• Race: Half-Elf
  • Faction: None
  • Location: Goslow
  • Building: The Bulkhead

Jarvis Aucien is a tall, blonde, and muscular Half-Elf who operates The Bulkhead in Goslow, a family rope and ship making business that has been passed down the Aucien line for generations. The Bulkhead is where anyone seeking the finest sea-faring vessels in all of Saros go, with hopes that they have enough coin, and that Jarvis’ services aren’t booked out more than a few months. There is also quite the ropemaking operation as well, situated right on the docks. The actual Aucien Shipyard is just outside the gates of Goslow on the coast of Bishop’s Bay to the north.

docs.title: Korth
docs.text: Korth serves as Head Priest at The Temple of Torm in Goslow. He is a very old and wise human paladin with large white eyebrows that hide his small eyes. Fairly narcoleptic and seems to always be asleep, however locals tell of a time when he was a mighty warrior who rallied the town to victory against a massive orc raiding horde.

docs.title: Lone Wolf Louie
docs.text: Overseer of “The Silver Drake” Gambler’s Guild hall. Speaks with a heavy accent and is always chewing on something which makes him somewhat hard to comprehend.

docs.title: Mary
docs.text: Mary is a sweet lady with a small-town charm not often felt in busy, bustling Goslow. Mary’s hobbies include raising butterflies, beekeeping, and spending most days sitting in the shade playing cards, gossiping with friends, reading “The Fine Point” gazette and drinking lemonade while her husband Bedford works the anvil. She dreams of one day being able to draw from the “Deck of Many Things”.

docs.title: Mirken Stanton
docs.text:
Captain of “The Storm Runner” (Small Troop Transport) Known for being fearless and ferocious when needed. Fair tempered but fast to fight especially when it comes to Breelyn, his Navigator. Strong disliking to pirates, but hates The Aegis Legion more. Claims to have the most dragon turtle kills on the high seas. Obsessed with the legendary Golden Grouper and has sworn to capture it.

“The Stormrunner” Ship Small Troop Transport 100 crewmen Captain Stanton Navigator Breelyn

Sworn Enemy: Admiral Thainan of The Aegis Legion Naval Fleet

docs.title: Mori
docs.text:
• Race: Half-Elf
  • Faction: None
  • Location: Goslow
  • Building: The Sphinx's Spellbook

The owner of The Sphinx’s Spellbook is a short female Half-Elf named Mori; a timid but extremely intelligent young woman with purple hair and alchemical tattoos all over her visible skin - except her face which is almost free of ink. Mori lives above the shop on the 2nd story with her pet penguin Chibs, who she rescued and healed after finding him alone, lost, and hurt in Bishop’s Bay several years ago.

docs.title: Munchies Muldridge
docs.text: Munchil “Munchies” Muldridge, nephew of Perla, works at The Toad and wants to adventure. Not very bright and often causing trouble in town that Perla has to clean up.

docs.title: Ostalda
docs.text: Ostalda is the resident sage that lives in a small room attached to the library inside of The Temple of Torm in Goslow. She is a Half-Elf with dark hair and bluing skin from years of divining with sacred mushrooms.

docs.title: Perla Mudridge
docs.text:
• Race: Halfling
  • Faction: None
  • Location: Goslow
  • Building: The Toad

The owner and innkeeper of The Toad, a tall female halfling named Perla. She was once an adventurer, but was maimed by a dragon and lost her left leg. Perla’s best friend is Gerdga who also happens to manage The Toad, and she employs and watches over her inept nephew Munchil “Munchies” Muldridge. She loves details, and she’s often seen sitting at a table drinking and eagerly sharing tales with adventurers that come into The Toad (with her Fey-stone leg propped up on the table).

docs.title: Vostin The Mighty
docs.text: Captain of The Aegis Legion in Goslow at Duskpoint. Known as Vostin The Mighty to most in Goslow, as he is rarely seen prostrating himself in front of anyone but General Ironclad or Queen Amara herself.

docs.title: Grymswatch
docs.text:
Headquarters and home of The Aegis Legion. Grymswatch serves as the realm’s military training ground, and it’s main defense against the pirate factions of Karastos, specifically The Bloodmarked pirates.

Population - 1000

docs.title: Mira's Wall
docs.text: The main headquarters and training facility for The Aegis Legion. Mira’s Wall is a massive castle-like structure and the central figure standing tall amongst the few low peasant homes that make up Grymswatch.

docs.title: Admiral Thainan
docs.text: Admiral of The Aegis Legion Naval Fleet and viscous lapdog of General Ironclad. Without the general’s approval and his record proving his usefulness against the legion’s enemies, he would likely be sentenced to death for the crimes he has committed against the realm in the name of “progress”. One of the most hated figures in all of Saros.

docs.title: Festin Dontel
docs.text: Sworn sword of Admiral Thainan, guard and Lieutenant of The Aegis Legion, and Second in Command at Grymswatch. Festin is not nearly as mean spirited as his counterpart. Many wish he was in command, as he garners more respect and camaraderie from his troops than Thainan ever could.

docs.title: Karastos
docs.text:
Pirate capital of Saros. Home to the Pirate Lord. Locked in a seemingly eternal conflict with The Aegis Legion outpost headquarters at Grymswatch.

docs.title: Kylor
docs.text:
A coastal bay village delicately poised on the ocean’s edge. Dominated by the art of fishing and boatsmithing, the city resonates with the rhythmic pulse of the sea. Kylor boasts a strong Legion presence, ensuring the safety of its shores from the threat of outsiders, but a danger to those who dare disobey any legion’s random whim.

Population - 450

docs.title: Port Quartz
docs.text:
Port Quartz is a crowded river town of approximately 5,250 permanent residents and one of the most important trade intersections in northern Saros.

It stands where established roads, immense rivers, ferry traffic, and southern shipping meet. There is no bridge across the principal river; Sarosian builders cannot practically span its width and current. Ferries are therefore the foundation of the town’s economy.

Port Quartz is the last dependable center of civilization before the isolated country northwest toward the Masys Mountains.

docs.title: Geography and routes
docs.text:
The principal safe roads are:

  • Southwest toward Goslow and Kylor
  • East toward Trystyn
  • North from Trystyn toward Lilya

There is no charted safe road north from Port Quartz to the Lake of Lament.

The Lake of Lament lies far above Port Quartz in the high basin around the Silvervein Summits. At its southwestern edge, the lake pours over an immense waterfall and feeds the southern river.

No vessel can travel from Port Quartz to the lake.

Explorers may cross west at Westwater Ferry and turn northwest toward Masys, but maintained paths disappear quickly.

docs.title: Government
docs.text:
Port Quartz is governed under royal charter by the Mooring Council, presided over by First Mooring Hesta Vane.

The five traditional responsibilities are:

  • First Mooring
  • Master of Ferries
  • Warden of the River Works
  • First Factor
  • Ward Speaker

The Mooring Council regulates ferries, salvage, warehouses, tariffs, guide licenses, emergency stores, and civic justice.

The local Aegis garrison is commanded by Captain Serin Holt. The garrison does not legally govern the town, though the Queen’s disappearance has encouraged increasingly broad claims of emergency authority.

docs.title: Trade and economy
docs.text:
Port Quartz’s wealth comes from movement rather than production.

Major trades include:

  • Ferry operation
  • Warehousing
  • Customs and cargo brokerage
  • Rivercraft repair
  • Cartage and animal handling
  • Rope, pitch, barrels, and tackle
  • Salvage
  • Northern expedition supply
  • Transfer of goods between Goslow, Trystyn, Lilya, and Rore

docs.title: Fall casks
docs.text:
Certain durable goods from Lilya and the Lake of Lament basin are packed into reinforced barrels known as fall casks.

The casks are sealed, padded, iron-banded, and sent down the waterfall. Catch crews recover survivors from the river near Port Quartz.

Typical cargo includes:

  • Ingots and ore samples
  • Durable tools
  • Stonework
  • Sealed pigments
  • Dried herbs
  • Alchemical substances
  • Small high-value goods

Fragile goods, people, animals, and ordinary trade travel by road through Trystyn.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
Port Quartz has three overlapping armed forces:

  • Chain Watch: civic officers responsible for the town and quays
  • Aegis garrison: Crown soldiers responsible for military and regional threats
  • Licensed quay guards: private guards employed by merchants and warehouses

During a serious attack, the town can raise a militia, close dock approaches, and coordinate ferries from Chainwatch.

docs.title: Character
docs.text:
Port Quartz is practical, crowded, loud, and accustomed to strangers.

Its residents respect competence more than rank. The river determines working hours, prices, law, and funerals. The town survives because its people understand that no authority—not the Crown, guilds, Legion, or Mooring Council—can command the water.

docs.title: Breakwater Registry
docs.text:
The Breakwater Registry licenses:

  • Ferry operators
  • Recovery crews
  • Wilderness guides
  • Surveyors
  • Professional escorts

It also records travelers who declare an intention to leave established roads.

The public board lists missing expeditions, river conditions, dangerous wildlife, closed landings, suspected bandits, escort requests, and reports of corrupted plants or animals.

docs.title: Cataract Yard
docs.text:
The Cataract Yard is the fortified fall-cask recovery complex above the main quays.

It contains:

  • Chain booms
  • Recovery cranes
  • Winches
  • Sorting platforms
  • Cooperages
  • Drying sheds
  • Inspection warehouses
  • A salvage court

Catch crews recover reinforced barrels sent down the great waterfall from the Lake of Lament basin.

After storms, the Yard may receive casks, trees, animal carcasses, wreckage, and debris at the same time.

docs.title: Chainwatch
docs.text:
Chainwatch is a squat fortified tower above the busiest ferry landings.

The civic watch uses it to:

  • Observe river traffic
  • Coordinate ferry signals
  • Close portions of the waterfront
  • Hold minor prisoners
  • Store unidentified river salvage

A heavy warning chain can be drawn across part of the lower harbor during emergencies using boats and shore-mounted capstans.

docs.title: Hall of Moorings
docs.text:
A low, broad pale-stone building near the principal quay.

The Hall serves as:

  • Town hall
  • Customs office
  • Civic courtroom
  • Mooring Council chamber
  • Cargo-record office
  • Emergency command center

Its main chamber contains a long table built from the timbers of the first chartered ferry.

Walls display river charts, flood lines, ferry schedules, and plaques naming vessels lost to the current.

docs.title: Quartz Vaults
docs.text:
The Quartz Vaults are secure warehouses cut into pale stone above the quays.

Upper chambers hold ordinary high-value cargo. Lower chambers are older than the current town, and several sealed doors have resisted every local locksmith.

The Mooring Council keeps separate chambers for confiscated cargo, emergency grain, civic records, and dangerous salvage.

docs.title: Shrine of the Last Oar
docs.text:
A small riverside sanctuary dedicated to those lost upon the water.

The interior contains carved names, broken oars, river stones, recovered possessions, and travelers’ offerings.

The shrine does not distinguish between Crown sailors, pirates, Black Circle travelers, merchants, or ordinary dead. Its neutrality makes it a quiet place for messages and meetings.

“Grief has no faction.”

docs.title: The Fourty Knights
docs.text: The Knights is the largest tavern and inn available in Port Quartz. Ran by Prance Mondrel, this inn has quite a few rooms to spare, though they’re not well kept. Thoughtful service and hospitality are in short supply at The Knight, as there are far too many travelers and far too much coin being passed around to take anything else into consideration.

docs.title: Vane Archive
docs.text:
The Vane Archive began as a family records room and became Port Quartz’s unofficial repository of exploration history.

Its holdings include:

  • Edric Vane’s surviving journals
  • Incomplete maps
  • Survey notes
  • Missing-person lists
  • Travelers’ accounts
  • Old ferry records
  • Reports of lost settlements
  • Recent Masys accounts from the last eighty years

The oldest records are valuable for terrain, rivers, ruins, and failed crossings. References plausibly connected to Rom or Mossback begin only within the last eighty years. Other old “moving hill” tales are catalogued separately and are not considered evidence of either one.

docs.title: Westwater Ferry
docs.text:
Westwater is the principal crossing for travelers arriving from Goslow and Kylor or departing toward the unsettled northwest.

The landing includes:

  • Heavy wagon ferries
  • Passenger boats
  • A fortified watch post
  • Stables
  • Equipment sellers
  • A return shrine
  • Missing-person notices
  • A marker honoring Edric Vane

The marker points northwest even though no maintained road continues in that direction.

docs.title: White Quays
docs.text:
The White Quays are Port Quartz’s principal waterfront, carved into broad shelves of pale quartz.

When wet, the stone reflects lantern light and appears faintly luminous.

Daily activity includes:

  • Ferry loading
  • Cargo weighing
  • Customs inspections
  • Rivercraft auctions
  • Animal handling
  • Ship and barge repair
  • Public arguments over salvage and tariffs

A signal bell system announces hazards, arrivals, closures, broken lines, and bodies recovered from the river.

docs.title: Caldus Renn
docs.text:
Caldus Renn is one of the few living guides known to have crossed the western rivers and returned from the Masys foothills.

He no longer accepts commissions.

Caldus walks with a stiff left leg and wears river stones tied into his bootlaces. He claims they remind him which side of a crossing he entered from.

docs.title: His final expedition
docs.text:
Caldus found:

  • Corrupted woodland
  • A circle of healthy flowers
  • A deliberate stone arrangement
  • A distant rounded shape gone the next day

Two companions vanished after following lights uphill.

docs.title: What he provides
docs.text:
• The safest known secondary-river crossing
  • A warning about misleading high-ground routes
  • The last useful cairn
  • Advice that healthy magical pockets are better guides than old roads

He will speak if Hesta sends the party, they show the corruption sample, Bastet manifests, or they promise to record what happened to the missing.

docs.title: Captain Serin Holt
docs.text:
Captain Serin Holt commands the Aegis garrison in Port Quartz.

Holt is controlled, observant, and trapped between the town’s charter and emergency orders issued since Queen Amara’s disappearance.

docs.title: Beliefs
docs.text:
• The crossing is strategically essential.
  • Hesta Vane’s resistance creates dangerous delays.
  • The Black Circle uses civic disagreement as cover.
  • Unpleasant Council orders are preferable to disorder.
  • Captain Vostin interprets commands too freely.

docs.title: Conflict with Hesta
docs.text:
Holt claims authority over:

  • Crown threats
  • Smuggling
  • Sedition
  • Military cargo
  • Wanted fugitives
  • Emergency closures

Hesta insists these powers do not erase Port Quartz law.

docs.title: Hidden uncertainty
docs.text:
Holt has seen northern orders that do not follow ordinary Legion procedure. He suspects corruption in the supply chain but fears admitting it will weaken the garrison.

He can become an obstacle, reluctant ally, record source, or antagonist. His danger comes from believing temporary authority can be surrendered later.

docs.title: Hesta Vane
docs.text:
Hesta Vane is the First Mooring of Port Quartz and the most powerful civic official in town.

A former ferry captain in her late fifties, Hesta is broad-shouldered, weathered, and missing two fingers from a chain accident. She dresses plainly and wears the ceremonial white cloak of office only when law or tradition demands it.

She is a direct descendant of Edric Vane, who led the famous expedition toward Masys centuries ago.

docs.title: Personality
docs.text:
Hesta is practical rather than warm. She believes nearly every political dispute eventually becomes a problem of food, transport, labor, or access.

She dislikes the heroic mythology surrounding Edric because she knows the cost of his expedition.

“Edric Vane went west with sixty people. Seven returned. The statues always leave that part off.”

docs.title: Authority
docs.text:
Hesta:

  • Presides over the Mooring Council
  • Confirms major ferry and salvage decisions
  • Commands the Chain Watch through civic officers
  • Controls access to protected expedition records
  • Defends the town’s charter against Legion overreach

She is not anti-Crown, but her loyalty is to Port Quartz before the Council, guilds, or Legion.

docs.title: Current conflict
docs.text:
Since Queen Amara’s disappearance, Captain Serin Holt has received orders encouraging broader emergency powers.

Hesta refuses to let the garrison:

  • Seize private boats without due process
  • Read the full expedition registry
  • Arrest residents solely for anti-Crown speech
  • Confiscate salvage without a hearing
  • Replace civic law with military convenience

docs.title: Adventure use
docs.text:
Hesta can provide:

  • Edric’s journal passage
  • A letter to Oren Bale
  • A Port Quartz writ
  • Access to private cargo records
  • Political protection from Captain Holt

She responds to competence, evidence, and honesty rather than claims of urgency.

docs.title: Nelra Vossin
docs.text:
Nelra Vossin keeps the Vane Archive.

She is meticulous, soft-spoken, and much more interested in whether a story is independent than whether it is dramatic.

docs.title: Work
docs.text:
Nelra compares:

  • Expedition journals
  • Ferry declarations
  • Missing-person notices
  • Old maps
  • Merchant ledgers
  • Tavern accounts recorded by clerks
  • Repeated legends under different names

She believes the scattered stories of Rom refer to one real individual who appeared in the Masys records only within the last eighty years.

docs.title: What she knows
docs.text:
• Edric Vane’s records are incomplete.
  • Several missing pages were copied before disappearing.
  • Accounts from the last eight decades describe a moving habitation near Hex 75.86.
  • Recent magical failures can be traced through expedition reports from the last few years.
  • Recent northwest accounts describe healthy clearings inside corrupted land.
  • Different witnesses from the last eighty years use several names for the same strange wizard.

Nelra can turn recent rumors into a usable route clue and expose false merchant paperwork. Edric Vane’s much older journals are useful for geography and crossings only; she explicitly rejects attempts to attribute old “moving hill” legends to Rom or Mossback.

docs.title: Oren Bale
docs.text:
Oren Bale is the senior ferrymaster at Westwater Ferry.

He decides when wagons, animals, and expeditions may cross the main river.

Oren is patient with fear and impatient with bravado.

He asks every northwest-bound traveler:

  • How many days of food they carry
  • Whether they can repair a boat
  • Whether they know the water level
  • Who should be told if they do not return

He knows where the maintained path ends, which landing avoids marsh ground, and how rain changes the secondary crossings.

“Once the river is behind you, every trail is somebody’s guess.”

docs.title: Prance Mondrel
docs.text: Owner and operator of The Fourty Knights tavern and inn located on the docks of Port Quartz. Prance is a very lazy man, and spends most days in his chair yelling at his servants and trying to explain the bug infestations to customers…

docs.title: Pyrris
docs.text:
The majestic capital of Saros, Pyrris perches atop a colossal cliffside, overlooking the sprawling expanse of the kingdom. Home to the illustrious Radiant Citadel, the city pulses with life, and its streets teem with a large traveler contingency seeking counsel and aid from the Queen. The only way to Pyrris is the High Road from Goslow.

Population - 500

docs.title: Stonepeak
docs.text: The Aegis Legion garrison at Pyrris, overseen by General Ironclad. Stonepeak lies at the foot of The Radiant Citadel and anyone passing through the gates must first pass it’s checkpoint.

docs.title: The Radiant Citadel
docs.text: Home to Queen Amara and the main seat of power in Saros. A shimmering white tower, raising into the clouds, resting on the edge of the high Pyrris cliffs that fall straight into the deep waters of Bishop’s Bay. Surrounded by a great wall patrolled by The Aegis Legion, the Citadel is heavily fortified and secure from all invasion forces from without.

docs.title: Ambassador Skylark
docs.text:
Queen’s Council member Leonora Skylark

Role: Envoy of Public Relations (Queen’s Hand)

   - A diplomatic and charismatic individual, Ambassador Leonora exudes warmth and friendliness. Her golden hair and bright smile give her a welcoming appearance, and her attire, adorned with symbols of diplomacy, reflects her commitment to fostering good relations.

   - Responsibility: Nurturing diplomatic relations with neighboring realms, handling foreign affairs, and managing the realm’s image on the international stage.

docs.title: Archmage Starweaver
docs.text:
Queen’s Council member Nisel Starweaver

Role: Minister of Arcane Affairs

   - A wise and serene-looking woman, Archmage Nisel possesses an otherworldly grace. Her silver hair is intricately braided, and her robes shimmer with subtle magical energies. She speaks with measured words, revealing a deep understanding of the arcane.

   - Responsibility: Managing magical affairs, overseeing the realm’s arcane institutions, and advising on matters related to magical diplomacy and defense.

docs.title: General Ironclad
docs.text:
Queen’s Council member Roland Ironclad Resides and commands from Stonepeak

Role: Supreme Commander of the Military

   - An imposing figure with a close-cropped beard and a weathered face, General Roland wears his military regalia with pride. His eyes, however, betray a keen intelligence, and his firm handshake belies a strategic mind.

   - Responsibility: Strategizing and overseeing the kingdom’s defense, commanding the military forces, and ensuring the realm’s security.

docs.title: Gormley
docs.text: The most famous bard in all of Saros, known for his wonderous skills in singing, dancing, juggling, magic, and tale-telling. He spends most months traveling to the Major Cities, Towns, and Ports, touring his newest songs to the wonder of all who have ears to hear them. In the spring months he has a residency at The Radiant Citadel, playing concerts throughout The Spring Harvest Festival, during which time he is also employed by The Queen as her personal entertainer to perform for guests at her nightly feasts.

docs.title: Lord Goldhaven
docs.text:
Queen’s Council member Cedric Goldhaven

Role: Treasurer and Keeper of Wealth

   - A distinguished older gentleman with salt-and-pepper hair, Lord Cedric wears finely tailored robes of deep burgundy. His piercing gaze hides a wealth of financial acumen, and his calm demeanor exudes an air of reliability.

   - Responsibility: Overseeing the kingdom’s finances, managing the royal treasury, and ensuring economic stability.

docs.title: Queen Amara
docs.text:
Queen Amara Tatami, the elven matriarch and wielder of powerful magic, is an ethereal and regal figure. The air around her seems to shimmer with residual magic, a testament to the immense power she commands. A harmonious blend of elven beauty, her celestial grace and arcane wisdom make her a figure of awe and reverence among her people in the realms of Saros.

Rumored to be: Imprisoned in the Tower of Pyrris Kidnapped by one of the many factions of Saros Overthrown by her Counsel Murdered

docs.title: Spymaster Shadowcloak
docs.text:
Queen’s Council member Elias Shadowcloak

Role: Minister of Espionage and Intelligence

   - Elias, with his quiet demeanor, blends into the shadows effortlessly. His dark clothing and observant eyes make him seem like a keen observer. He often appears in places one wouldn’t expect, his movements swift and deliberate.

   - Responsibility: Operating covert operations, gathering intelligence, and ensuring the realm’s safety through subterfuge and discreet information gathering.

docs.title: Skaggerty
docs.text:
A small crossroads town settling between the junctions of Kylor, Goslow, and the road to The Masys Mountains.

Population - 280

docs.title: Temple of Austerus
docs.text:
A Temple dedicated to Austerus “The Shining One” located in Skaggerty. Deity of redemption and holy light, formerly the fiendish deity of searing radiance, now turned to Order. Seeks to bring all of humanity under one rule.

Heldoren The Wise oversees the daily operations of the Temple.

docs.title: The Stout Fool
docs.text:
Ran by Simoon, a diminutive and unassuming human male with quite an intellect and a dark sense of humor. He lives above the Stout Fool in one of the only few available rooms.

Rooms: (per night) Modest (1 sp) = 3 Accommodating (5 sp) = 1

docs.title: Heldoren The Wise
docs.text: The high priest who oversees the Temple of Austerus in Skaggerty. An elderly, withered man, short and bent with age, barely able to support his own weight with his cane. Besides carrying out general priestly duties, he also takes on the role of sage due to the low population of the town.

docs.title: Simoon
docs.text: Owner and proprietor of The Stout Fool, the only tavern and inn in Skaggerty. A diminutive but brash human male with quite the intellect and a dark sense of humor. He lives above The Fool in one of only a few small rooms.

docs.title: Delves
docs.text:
Long ago in the 2nd Age when magical knowledge was crude at best, the Dwarves and Elves worked together to harness the powers emanating from the earth at specific points known as Fey-Lines. These fey-lines were loosely connected magical streams that seemed to flow between one another and converge at specific points all across Saros. Where any lines met there would form great places of magical energy.

The elves used this magical power to spread life and abundance upon the lands, to keep their realms hidden from unknown dangers and eventually other races as their distrust grew. The dwarves used their great knowledge of architecture and geometry to set up massive “Delves” to both mine the Sarosian soil for the wonderous gems and “Fey-stone”, and to set up remote bases of operations for each mountain-home’s ruling clan.

Many of these “delves” are now lost to time and ruin, likely occupied by denizens of the deeps that the dwarves unleased by digging too greedily. Once a delve inevitably goes too deep it is sealed, yet there is rumor of great untold treasure and magic to be uncovered by any who happen to discover these once majestic dwarven structures hidden underground, should they make it back to see the suns again.

There are a few delves in Saros whose locations are known, and even one delve that has caused an entire town to spring up around it. Once a delve has been re-found, it isn’t long before adventurers of all types come seeking gold and glory, which usually sees traders and merchant-types follow along to pick up the scraps.

docs.title: Goslow Delve
docs.text:
Recently re-discovered and unsealed by an unknown source, a dwarf at The Toad has been leading adventurers into the cave entrance to the Delve under the assumption that his original party is all but lost down there.

A party of adventurers thwarted The Prism’s attempt to open the 2nd level of the delve that was sealed by magic centuries ago.

docs.title: Port Quartz Delve
docs.text: Located in Port Quartz, this Delve is heavily guarded by The Aegis Legion. Not many adventurers are allowed inside unless approved by the Port Quartz authority.

docs.title: Tomb of The Serpent King
docs.text: A once prosperous and esteemed underground city of Snake-men led by the fearless Serpent King. Now fallen to age and ruin… home to Xiximanter, goblins, and blue mushrooms. Located a few miles south of Goslow.

docs.title: The Glimmering Expanse
docs.text:
The vast central region of Saros that is largely uninhabitable due to the harsh conditions presented. Rumored to have been created in the 1st Age during a great dragon war, the Expanse is mostly desert and sand, with shards of glass littering the landscape, sometimes culminating in massive crystalline glass formations jutting out from the ground. The wind blows at such a speed that it stirs up clouds of sand-glass and tears apart anything not well prepared for the assault.

The only connection between northern and southern Saros is the land-bridge that spans the expanse over a great canyon known as The Wyrm Scar. The Wyrm Scar cuts through the entire continent, splitting the two hemispheres apart almost entirely and uniting the two major waters of The Sea of Myth and The Sparkling Sea. Passage over the land-bridge is thought to be impossible since the disappearance of the Khaz’armok, who at one time were the inhabitants and guides through The Expanse.

docs.title: The Wyrm Scar
docs.text:
A massive river canyon that cuts through the entire continent of Saros, splitting the two hemispheres apart almost entirely and uniting the two major waters of The Sea of Myth and The Sparkling Sea. Passage through the Scar is treacherous but not impossible, as it takes patience and skillful navigation to get around the glass and rock that litters the canyon.

Many believe the Wyrm Scar and The Glimmering Expanse were created in the 1st Age during a great dragon war.

docs.title: R1. House Rules
docs.text:
1. No class/race restrictions & No bonus XP a. As long as the player can come up with a good reason for any strange combo… b. Bonus XP modifiers will not be used.

  2. Characters start with max HP a. Add CON +/- modifier. Players will still roll for HP at each level up.

  3. Slot-based inventory system a. Each character has an inventory of 10 slots +STR modifier bonus. b. Armor worn and weapons carried do not take up inventory slots. c. 100 coins = 1 slot / 1h items = 1 slot / 2h items = 2 slots / light armor = 1 slot / heavy armor = 2 slots / very small items = free carry / other items = referee’s discretion.

  4. Magic Users a. Start with: Read Magic, Light. b. Casting “Reversed: Darkness” still requires training in the Light spell. c. May use staffs regardless of class weapon restrictions.

  5. Fighters a. Cleave: Any time a fighter strikes a killing blow in melee they may immediately roll a free attack against another adjacent enemy within range. This can chain. b. May select a combat talent at 1st, 5th, and 10th level from the optional table (C.C. #1 page 28).

  6. Druids a. Start with: Speak With Animals

  7. Thief a. Optional rules from C.C. 1 page 29.

  8. Splintering Shields a. Characters can choose to destroy their shield rather than take the damage on a hit from a weapon or similar physical trap/spell/monster attack. b. If a shield is destroyed this way, the character incurs the “Fractured” de-buff. c. The “Fractured” de-buff causes characters to suffer a -2 AC and be unable to use their shield arm. d. The “Fractured” de-buff is removed when a character has fully rested and their HP returned to full.

  9. Downed, Recover, Wounded, and Character Death a. When reduced to 0HP characters enter a “Downed” state of 1. b. “Downed” characters can only perform a “Recover” roll (Save VS Death) on their turn. c. Recover Fail = Add 1 stack of “Downed”. Recover Success = Character moves to “Wounded” state. d. “Wounded” characters are returned to 1HP and are marked with the “Wounded” de-buff. This de-buff can stack. e. Healing a “Downed” character will return them to “Wounded” state. The heal restores HP as normal. f. The “Wounded” de-buff is removed when a character has fully rested and their HP returned to full. g. “Wounded” x3 / “Downed” x4 = instant death. ANY damage vs “Downed” = instant death. h. If at any time a character’s HP would be reduced by -10 + their character level they are instantly killed.

docs.text: If you aren’t feeling it, it’s okay to take a break or even sit out a session or two.

docs.title: 8. No Grandstanding / Session De-railing
docs.text:
Everyone will get their turn to be a hero. We are all here together so please try and focus on the game and honor the collective experience of others.

Everyone is welcome in Saros. If you can not agree to these rules this game/server is not for you.
